 December fuel price forecast: Petrol cuts on the way
 Early December fuel price projections suggest petrol relief for South African motorists, but diesel could get more expensive.
 November 9, 2026 
  | 
 by 
 Thandi Selepe 
 |  Follow us on Google News 
 South African motorists could see significant petrol price cuts in December 2026, although diesel drivers may not be as lucky.
 Early figures from the Central Energy Fund (CEF) suggest petrol could fall by more than R1.50 per litre when the new prices take effect on Wednesday, 2 December.
 However, these are preliminary estimates. Final adjustments will depend on international oil prices, the rand, and government levies over the rest of November.
 How much could petrol and diesel prices change? 
 Based on early November CEF data, with the government’s scheduled fuel levy changes included, the projections are:
 Petrol 93: A decrease of approximately R1.52 per litre.
 Petrol 95: A decrease of approximately R1.82 per litre.
 Diesel 500ppm: Up about R1.49 per litre.
 Diesel 50ppm: Up about R1.15 per litre.
 The figures are early forecasts and could change considerably before the end of November.
 Why could petrol become cheaper? 
 Two factors are helping motorists: lower international oil prices and a stronger rand against the US dollar.
 South Africa imports much of its fuel, so changes in global oil prices and the exchange rate directly influence what drivers pay at the pumps.
 The government introduced temporary fuel levy relief in November to cushion consumers against rising costs.
 From December, that relief will be reduced, effectively adding 50 cents per litre to petrol and R1.50 per litre to diesel compared with November’s levy rates.
 This is why diesel could become more expensive despite improving international fuel-price conditions.
 When will December’s fuel prices take effect? 
 South Africa’s next fuel price adjustment is scheduled for Wednesday, 2 December 2026.
 The Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources is expected to announce the final prices shortly before then.
 Until that announcement, the figures remain forecasts, not guaranteed savings or increases.
 For now, petrol drivers have reason to be cautiously optimistic. Diesel users, however, will be hoping for further improvements before the December prices are finalised.
